answer: A marketplace can price trust like timber, jade, and crystal grades instead of counting identities. Every agent stakes a refundable deposit before listing services; the stake is locked in escrow and slashed when peers prove fraud. One fake identity costs one full stake, so a Sybil swarm must pay for every copy, while honest agents earn their deposit back plus fees. Attackers face a linear, upfront cost per identity, turning cheap identity forgery into an expensive, losing trade.
